questions.q: How many days are in a leap year?
questions.e: A leap year has an extra day, 29 February.

questions.q: How many letters are in the English alphabet?
questions.e: There are 26 letters from A to Z.

questions.q: What colour do you get by mixing red and white?
questions.e: Red and white make pink.

questions.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.e: Hex means six.

questions.q: What is 12 x 12?
questions.e: 12 times 12 is 144.

questions.q: A word that reads the same backwards, like "level", is called a...
questions.e: Palindromes read the same in both directions.

questions.q: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
questions.e: A standard guitar has six strings.

questions.q: Which continent has no permanent human population?
questions.e: Only scientists live temporarily in Antarctica.

questions.q: What is the Roman numeral for 50?
questions.e: L stands for 50.

questions.q: What is the smallest prime number?
questions.e: 2 is the smallest and the only even prime.

questions.q: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.e: Mandarin has the most native speakers.

questions.q: What is 15% of 200?
questions.e: 10% of 200 is 20 and 5% is 10, so 30.

questions.q: Which number greater than 1 is both a perfect square and a perfect cube?
questions.e: 64 = 8 x 8 and 4 x 4 x 4.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.e: Mars looks red because of iron oxide dust.

questions.q: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
questions.e: The heart is a muscular pump.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.e: Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.e: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun.

questions.q: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.e: Diamond is the hardest natural material.

questions.q: Which force keeps us on the ground?
questions.e: Gravity pulls objects towards the Earth.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.e: Au comes from the Latin word aurum.

questions.q: How many bones does an adult human body have?
questions.e: Adults have 206 bones.

questions.q: Who proposed the theory of relativity?
questions.e: Albert Einstein published it in the early 1900s.

questions.q: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.e: About 78% of the air is nitrogen.

questions.q: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
questions.e: Fleming noticed mould killing bacteria.

questions.q: Roughly how fast does light travel?
questions.e: Light moves at about 300,000 km every second.

questions.q: What does DNA stand for?
questions.e: DNA carries genetic information.

questions.q: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.e: The stapes is only about 3 mm long.

questions.q: What is the pH of pure water at room temperature?
questions.e: A pH of 7 is neutral.

questions.q: Which animal is the fastest on land?
questions.e: Cheetahs can reach about 100 km/h in short bursts.

questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.e: Spiders have eight legs; insects have six.

questions.q: What is the largest animal on Earth?
questions.e: Blue whales are the largest animals ever known.

questions.q: What is a group of lions called?
questions.e: Lions live in prides.

questions.q: Which is the tallest animal?
questions.e: Giraffes can be over 5 metres tall.

questions.q: Which is the only mammal capable of true flight?
questions.e: Bats are the only mammals that truly fly.

questions.q: What is the process by which a caterpillar becomes a butterfly?
questions.e: Metamorphosis means a complete change of form.

questions.q: Which food famously almost never spoils?
questions.e: Honey can last for thousands of years.

questions.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.e: Two pump blood to the gills and one to the body.

questions.q: Botanically, a banana is classified as a...
questions.e: Botanists classify bananas as berries.

questions.q: The Sun is a star.
questions.e: The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system.

questions.q: Sound travels faster than light.
questions.e: Light is vastly faster, which is why you see lightning before thunder.

questions.q: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
questions.e: Tall objects are often struck many times.

questions.q: A tomato is botanically a fruit.
questions.e: Tomatoes develop from the flower's ovary, so they are fruit.

questions.q: Humans use only 10% of their brains.
questions.e: This is a myth; we use virtually all of our brain.

questions.q: Goldfish only have a three-second memory.
questions.e: Goldfish can remember things for months.
